title: access_invite
description: The facts the message kind access_invite (you are invited to the Console) can use. A fact schema is the one definition of what a template of this kind may mention: the Console offers exactly these as placeholders and the checker refuses any other. Facts marked x_derived are worked out by the kind's fact builder in the product, not typed by anyone and not computed by the template.

x_kind.name: Access invite (you are invited to the Console)
triggers: Someone is invited in Access (a new access person is saved): sent automatically, once.
An operator presses Resend invite email on a person in Access: sent again, by hand (manual sends ignore duplicate protection).
x_kind.recipient: adhoc: the Google email on the access person, and their name when one is given. An access person is not an individual record.
x_kind.dedupe: explicit key: kind + access person id (the automatic send happens once per person; Resend is manual)
refs: none: the person invited is an access person, not one of the records a log entry links to (request, class, attendance). The log entry's address and subject identify the send.

name.description: How the email greets the person: the first word of the name given on the invitation, else the word there.

inviter.description: Who sent the invitation: the inviter's name when they signed in with Google and have a name on file, else their Google email, else (the admin key) the words The LAUNCH team.

role_name.description: The label of the role the person was given, as shown in Access.

role_description.description: What that role is for, in the role's own words (its description in Access). Absent when the role has none.
examples: Runs classes and requests in their own regions.

email.description: The Google address they must sign in with (the address on the invitation).

console_url.description: The address of the Console. Public; never carries a key or a token.
